newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Celesc still a Caspian buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Celesc still a Caspian buy.

text.p: Caspian Securities said Tuesday it had reiterated its buy rating on state-owned power distributor Celesc based on its inexpensive valuation and likely privatization in 1999.

-- Caspian analysts F. Rowe Michels and Alison Graham said the threatened impeachment of Santa Catarina state's Gov. Paulo Alfonso Vieira, who planned to introduce a privatization bill in March, will likely delay the selloff until after the October 1998 elections.

-- "If Vieira were removed before the next elections, the PMDB party's vice governor, Jose Augusto Hulse, would take over but would lack political support to pass the privatization bill," they wrote in a report.

-- They said Celesc is likely to be auctioned after elections because the two strongest gubernatorial candidates support selling off state assets and the state needs to repay debts to the federal government.
-- "The state's only option raising these funds is the sale of banking, electricity and water utility assets," the analysts said.

-- Celesc currently trades at 8.4 times estimated 1997 earnings, a 16 percent discount to the average for Brazilian distributors, and at an earnings-per-megawatt-hours-sold ratio of $110, a 48 percent discount to the average.
-- Common shares of Celesc were up 7.69 percent at 1,04 reais at 1300 local/1200 EDT/1600 GMT in Sao Paulo.
